confirmed: The source is the published journal article by Yi Wang and Chandra Mohan Vasudeva Panicker, Edelweiss Applied Science and Technology 9(6), 2790-2814 (2025), DOI 10.55214/25768484.v9i6.8493, published 1 July 2025; the PDF has 25 pages. The entire markdown, through the references, was read; no appendix is included and no supplementary material is identified (PDF p. 1, publication header/history; p. 25, end matter).

Reported randomization is explicit: Figure 1 says "Group Division / Randomized Assignment", and the text below Table 1 says the randomization procedure created comparable groups (PDF pp. 5 and 7; journal pp. 2794 and 2796). The design is also called quasi-experimental (PDF pp. 5-6, Section 3.1); the allocation method and unit are not specified. The form correctly flags this conflict for two-screener review rather than treating the study as observational context.

field_rct is supported as the reported design because the intervention occurred within real educational settings; context_class=none is appropriate. This is an original human-assistance study, not AI-versus-human output research or a synthesis (PDF p. 6, Section 3.1; pp. 13 and 15, Tables 5-6).

Figure 1 reports 120 students and 60 assigned per arm; Tables 5 and 6 report 60 analyzed per arm. These are people counts, so the main study exceeds the 50-person threshold. The separate 28-student instrument pilot is explicitly outside the primary study and has no reported randomized assistance comparison; exclusions/attrition are not stated (PDF p. 5, Figure 1; p. 6, Sections 3.2-3.3; pp. 13 and 15, Tables 5-6).
Participants came from four music institutions in Guangdong Province; Table 1 gives ages 17-24, mean 19.6, and sophomore, junior, and senior grade levels (PDF p. 6, Section 3.3; p. 7, Table 1).

AICP is described as integrating generative artificial neural networks; the curriculum contains five modules over a stated 12-week intervention. Figure 1 places post-intervention assessment in weeks 13-14 (PDF p. 6, Section 3.2; pp. 8-9, Section 4.1 and Table 2; p. 5, Figure 1).

CPAR assesses nine dimensions of compositions. The rating scale is 1-5, and Table 7 specifies five expert evaluators; Creative Fluency is a rating, not a reported count of generated ideas, so the form's construct=other is supported (PDF p. 6, Section 3.2; p. 14, Table 5 note; p. 20, Table 7 note).

S1-O1 and the one-line finding match: post-test Overall Creativity is experimental 4.71 (SD 0.54) versus control 3.62 (SD 0.69), n=60 each, mean difference 1.09, t=9.72, p<.001*, Cohen's d=1.77; pre-test values are 3.07 (0.68) versus 3.12 (0.72) (PDF p. 15, Table 6; p. 13, Table 5).

S1-O2 matches: post-test Melodic Originality is experimental 4.85 (SD 0.62) versus control 3.82 (SD 0.75), n=60 each, mean difference 1.03, t=8.42, p<.001*, Cohen's d=1.54; pre-test values are 3.42 (0.76) versus 3.38 (0.71) (PDF p. 15, Table 6; p. 13, Table 5).

S1-O3 matches: post-test Creative Fluency is experimental 4.83 (SD 0.61) versus control 3.58 (SD 0.75), n=60 each, mean difference 1.25, t=10.24, p<.001*, Cohen's d=1.87; pre-test values are 3.08 (0.82) versus 3.12 (0.79) (PDF p. 15, Table 6; p. 13, Table 5).

The with_ai classification has the support and limitation already noted in the form: the experimental works are labeled AI-assisted, but the paper gives no explicit post-test access/removal protocol. No unassisted post-removal assessment is described (PDF p. 18, Section 5.3; p. 20, Table 7 note; pp. 5-6, research methods).

The Figure 6 discrepancy is real: its experimental/control annotations are 29/1, 15/15, 16/14, and 0/30 across successive quartiles, whereas the accompanying prose gives 27/3, 22/8, 9/21, and 2/28 (PDF p. 22, journal p. 2811, Figure 6 visually checked and text below).

MANCOVA is described in the methods but no MANCOVA results are reported; the extracted effects come from the independent-samples post-test comparisons in Table 6. There are no synthesis study counts, pooled estimates, or pooled intervals to extract (PDF p. 7, Section 3.4; pp. 12-23, Section 5).
summary: The full text reports randomized assignment of 120 music students to AI-assisted or traditional composition instruction, so it needs two-screener review despite its conflicting quasi-experimental label. All three extracted results and the one-line finding match the PDF, but six rubric dimensions, the composite outcome, and contrast metadata are missing.
